rationale: Both designs share the right core: generation is separated from grading, blobs are content-addressed, records are append-only, regrades are new records against the same outputs, schema_version is dispatched on read, and derived indexes are rebuildable. B adds useful operational detail: checkpointing, partial runs, required grader-version filters and supersedes links. However, B's identity model has a real flaw. Its generation blob embeds run_id and created_at but excludes them from the hash, so a deduplicated blob carries the first run's run_id. B's reconstruct() then follows gen['run_id'] and can attribute an output to the wrong run. It also reads a content_uri field the evaluation record does not contain. A keeps the run-to-output mapping in the run manifest and keeps blobs free of run identity. It stores the grader's actual input as well as its output, gives a fully hash-linked reconstruction chain, verifies hashes on read, and records env snapshots and Docker digests for provenance. Its only error is cosmetic: a duplicated prompt hash in an example. A's design is more internally consistent and its reconstruction guarantee is sounder.
